In the cervical spinal cord of ALS patients versus controls (138 ALS, 36 Control, postmortem bulk RNA-seq), 6,534 genes are differentially expressed at FDR < 0.05 (edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test). At a biologically meaningful effect-size threshold (|log2FC| ≥ 1.0, FDR < 0.05), 128 genes are upregulated and 74 genes are downregulated in ALS.

The dominant transcriptional signature is neuroinflammation and glial activation. Pathway enrichment of upregulated genes reveals strong activation of the complement cascade (11/200 genes, padj = 1.1 × 10⁻⁶), inflammatory response (9/200, padj = 4.9 × 10⁻⁵), TNFα signaling via NF-κB (7/200, padj = 1.5 × 10⁻³), and KRAS signaling (12/200, padj = 2.1 × 10⁻⁷). Downregulated genes are depleted in neuronal system and cholinergic synapse pathways, consistent with motor neuron loss.

The top protein-coding DEG is GPNMB (log2FC = +2.74, padj = 8.9 × 10⁻¹⁹), a microglial activation marker and ALS GWAS risk gene. Other top upregulated genes include CTSS (cathepsin S), PLA2G7, HGF, ABCA1, MS4A7, TNFSF8, and HEXB — all associated with microglial/macrophage function, lysosomal activity, and lipid metabolism. The top downregulated gene is SNORD3C (log2FC = -6.07, padj = 5.5 × 10⁻²⁹), a small nucleolar RNA.

These findings implicate activated microglia, complement-mediated synapse elimination, and dysregulated lipid/lysosomal processing as molecular drivers of ALS pathology in the spinal cord. The pro-inflammatory glial signature is the strongest and most consistent transcriptional change, supporting therapeutic strategies targeting neuroinflammation in ALS.

Caveats: Covariate adjustment for genotype PCs was not directly incorporated into the DEG model due to software limitations (pydeseq2 non-functional; pyDEG edgeR API supports two-group comparison only). While age, sex, and library preparation were balanced between groups, gPC1 and gPC2 showed significant case-control imbalance (p = 0.0009 and p = 0.0176, respectively). Top DEGs were verified not to be correlated with gPC1 (all |r| < 0.12). The analysis used edgeR QL F-test as the primary method after confirming pydeseq2 incompatibility on this system.

## Delegation

I routed this task to **`bulk_rna_analyst`** — the Bulk RNA-seq Analyst, whose `use_when` line covers "拿到 bulk RNA-seq 表达矩阵(counts/TPM)...任何'哪些基因与某个样本变量相关 / 关联 / 差异表达'的问题都归这里."

**Data**: 174 postmortem cervical spinal cord samples (138 ALS, 36 Control) from the Zenodo record 6385747 ALS transcriptomics dataset, with 15,154 genes tested.

**Method**: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test via `ov.bulk.pyDEG.deg_analysis(method='edger')` (count-based negative-binomial; DESeq2 attempted but pydeseq2 v0.5.2 hung during `DeseqDataSet` construction on this system).
